videos.title: History of Banking in India + 120 Rules of Grammar (Rules 1-3) | IBPS & RRB SO IT 2026 Preparation
videos.description:
Welcome back to the channel! In this daily study vlog, I document Day 1 of my dedicated self-study preparation for the RRB SO IT & IBPS SO IT examinations while managing a full-time office job.

In this session, we cover core revision notes across two essential subjects:
1. Banking Awareness: Complete History of Indian Banking (Pre-Independence, Presidency Banks, Joint Stock Banks, Establishment of RBI, Nationalisation Phases 1 & 2, and RRBs).
2. English Grammar: 120 Rules of Grammar by Nimisha Bansal Ma'am (Rules 1, 2, and 3 covering Each vs Every, Both & And combinations, and Who vs Whom).

Timestamps / Chapters:
00:00 - Introduction & Daily Study Routine Plan
01:29 - Definition of Banking & Section 5(b) Banking Regulation Act 1949
02:07 - History of Banking in India (Pre-Independence & Presidency Banks)
03:19 - Joint Stock Banks (Bank of Upper India, Allahabad Bank)
04:02 - Oudh Commercial Bank, PNB & Central Bank of India (Swadeshi Movement)
05:07 - Merger vs Amalgamation & Imperial Bank of India (1921)
05:46 - Hilton Young Commission & RBI Act 1934 Establishment
07:32 - Imperial Bank Conversion to State Bank of India (SBI 1955)
08:00 - Bank Nationalisation Waves (Phase 1: 1969 & Phase 2: 1980)
08:48 - Regional Rural Banks (RRB 1975) & Shareholding Ratio (50:35:15)
10:15 - Financial Inclusion & 1991 LPG Reforms
11:21 - Old vs New Generation Commercial Banks & Neo Banks
12:08 - Indian Banking Structure: Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) & Foreign Banks
15:45 - 120 Rules of Grammar: Study Strategy & Overview
16:40 - Rule 1: 'Each' vs 'Every' & Abstract Nouns Explained
19:23 - Rule 2: Usage of 'Both' with 'And' (Avoiding 'As Well As' & 'Not')
20:48 - Rule 3: 'Who' (Subjective) vs 'Whom' (Objective) with Practice Examples
23:08 - Daily Summary & Tomorrow's Plan (DBMS Part 1 & NBFCs)

videos.title: Transmission Modes in 30 Seconds ⚡ Simplex vs Half-Duplex vs Full-Duplex | CS/IT Exams
videos.description:
In this Computer Networks Short, we quickly understand the 3 Data Transmission Modes:

🔹 Simplex – Communication in only one direction
📺 Example: TV Broadcasting

🔹 Half-Duplex – Two-way communication, but one direction at a time
📻 Example: Walkie-Talkie

🔹 Full-Duplex – Two-way communication simultaneously
📞 Example: Telephone Call

This is an important Computer Networks / Data Communication concept for Computer Science and IT competitive exams.
